summary: Frontend-only check of every modal on desktop (1366x650, 1920x950) plus an extra small-height stress test (1366x480) and an iPad landscape regression (1180x820), on tenant Pizzeria Napoli. Each modal got the provided DOM detector, an extended version of it, a mouse-wheel scroll over the card and a check of the last control and the primary button (visible + elementFromPoint hit test). RESULT: 0 unreachable elements in all 24 modals or modal states at every size. Every scrollable modal scrolled to the very bottom with the wheel, and the last control was clickable. The fixed footers dish-save-button, customer-save-button and create-order-button stayed visible without scrolling, both before and after the wheel scroll. iPad regression passed: a TEST_ dish was created through the dish modal and an order through the Nuovo Ordine modal, which then opened the add-item full-screen modal. The audit did turn up some contrast bugs and minor issues inside modals (see design_issues).

critical_code_review_comments: A whole family of white-on-white text (#ffffff on light backgrounds) looks left over from a dark-to-light theme switch. Grep for color: '#ffffff' / '#fff' on light backgrounds across the tabs

The provided detector only covers button/[role=button]/input/textarea. RN-Web Touchables render as div[tabindex=0] without role, so I also ran an extended detector that includes [tabindex=0]. It found 0 unreachable elements as well
index.tsx is over 4500 lines and should be split into modules

success_rate.frontend: 100% modal reachability (24/24 modal states, 3 desktop sizes + iPad); 3 contrast bugs inside modals
